## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T659 (seven fascicles; Sanskrit *Ratnameghasūtra*) is the slightly later joint translation by [曼陀羅仙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BC%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%99) (Mandrasena) and [僧伽婆羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85) (Saṅghabhara, 460–524) of the same Indic *Ratnamegha* underlying [T658](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0296). The two Funanese monks worked together at Jiànkāng under the Liáng, and the present text is the more polished of their two collaborative renderings — Saṅghabhara's longer Chinese residence having given him better command of literary Chinese.

**Abstract**

[僧伽婆羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85) (Saṅghabhara, *Sēngjiāpóluó*; 460–524; Skt. *Saṅghapāla* or *Saṃghabhara*) was the senior Funanese monk in the Liáng court and the longer-resident of the pair; he was active as a translator under both [梁武帝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A2%81%E6%AD%A6%E5%B8%9D) Liáng emperor Wǔ and earlier patrons. His Chinese was significantly more polished than Mandrasena's. Date bracket: 503 (joint activity with Mandrasena begins) to 524 (Saṅghabhara's death); the *[Lìdài sānbǎo jì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011)* (T2034) places the joint translation within this window. The text differs from [T658](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0296) in finer points of Chinese diction and chapter division but is essentially the same Indic source. The "Mahāyāna" prefix in the title (*Dàshèng* 大乘) reflects a later editorial decision to mark the doctrinal content rather than a different Indic source.

The Tang re-translation by [Dharmaruci](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF), [T660](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0298), is the most expanded of the three Chinese versions and reflects a different (later) Indic recension.
